transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been having a hard time at work. I clean buildings, and lately just the thought that I might see a rat—like in an old building or a trash room—gets me so worked up that I can’t do parts of my job. I know it’s probably not really dangerous, and I feel kind of silly saying it, but it’s gotten bad enough that I thought I should talk to someone.
Do you feel anxious mostly when you’re in places where you might see a rat, or do you also feel anxious in other situations that aren’t related to seeing rats?

Mostly it’s when I think there might be rats, yes. Like old buildings, trash rooms, places like that. I don’t think I’m just anxious everywhere, at least not that I’ve noticed. It’s really the thought of seeing one that kind of takes over, even though I know it probably isn’t actually dangerous.
